purpose: Test whether typed Semantic IR with stable obligation and AST identities, explicit loss, deterministic lowering, actual target validation, and dependency-local repair improves fresh Python maintenance outcomes for the exact frozen local model.

selected_claim.causal_variable: Typed source-to-semantic-to-target lowering with stable obligation and AST identities, explicit loss or ambiguity, actual target validation, and dependency-local repair.
selected_claim.selection_basis: P3 observed 12 incorrect outcomes among 14 independently evaluated typed edits plus 6 malformed outputs, while direct and integrated each solved 1 of 10 tasks. This is the preregistered translation-or-repair residual.

semantic_ir_contract.source_identity: stable digest of exact allowed source files
semantic_ir_contract.target_identity: AST node id plus exact source-segment SHA-256
semantic_ir_contract.obligation_identity: prospectively assigned IDs over request-visible requirements, preservation constraints, and non-goals
semantic_ir_contract.lowering: deterministic AST-identity-to-line-edit lowering against the exact original snapshot
semantic_ir_contract.loss: explicit NONE or unresolved obligation IDs; unresolved loss cannot release a candidate
semantic_ir_contract.repair: second complete IR against the original snapshot; changed units must remain within the dependency closure implicated by actual validation feedback
semantic_ir_contract.actual_target_validation: apply lowered action to a disposable original snapshot and execute the identical visible verifier

compiler_only_control.label: deterministic_request_compiler_baseline
compiler_only_control.input: only the natural request, allowed source snapshot, and allowed paths
fixed_rules: unique single-line exact literal replacement explicitly named with backticks
add or remove an explicitly named AST collection-literal element from an explicitly named symbol
compiler_only_control.purpose: Measure what a fixed, visible-request-only deterministic compiler can solve without learned generation.

compiler_oracle_ceiling.label: deterministic_compiler_oracle_ceiling
compiler_oracle_ceiling.input: sealed hand-authored oracle Semantic IR derived from the exact upstream target
compiler_oracle_ceiling.purpose: Prove target reachability, lowerer adequacy, validator sensitivity, and the deterministic lowering ceiling.

decision_rule.minimum_development_survivor_effect: typed Semantic IR must solve at least two more of ten tasks than direct generation, natural-language planning, and the prospective deterministic request-compiler control; lose on no more than one task against either learned control; and introduce zero unsafe or rollback failures
decision_rule.mechanics_floor: compiler oracle 10 of 10 useful; all four corruption classes rejected; at least 8 of 10 treatment IRs parse and lower; every treatment candidate binds model-generated IR and actual validation
decision_rule.cost_rule: all learned arms receive six total calls per task collectively and two each; report latency and total calls without hiding compiler or validation cost
decision_rule.negative_scope: A null or loss applies only to this exact bounded Python Semantic IR, model, task distribution, budget, validator, and repair policy; it cannot falsify cognitive compilation generally.

hosted_reference.future_extension: If a governed callable transport binds, freeze a separate identical-information P4 row before calls and keep local and hosted denominators separate.

maximum_inference: A terminal P4 result can decide only whether this exact bounded Semantic IR implementation is a development survivor for one fresh D1 qualification. It cannot establish a general cognitive-compilation claim, any synthesis claim, serving qualification, or book support transition.
